product_from_film: HydraDB is presented as context storage for AI that keeps relationships, decisions and changes over time to improve retrieval.
explains_well: The wrong-book and right-book library analogy makes the difference between a matching term and a relevant answer easy to follow.
unclear: The film never returns to its opening customer-contract question with a corrected answer and source, so the product benefit stays mostly metaphorical.
scenario: A wrong contract answer leads to a library analogy, then a context-storage diagram and a founder explanation.
product_clear_basis: The script explicitly says HydraDB stores actual context at 52s, with relationships and temporal details in the following diagram; the earlier library story explains a general retrieval problem.

scenes.action: A founder, laptop and prompt ask for the latest request on an Acme contract. The response instead names Apex Technologies. Abstract intelligence graphics and a NOT FOUND state support the wrong-document explanation.
scenes.design: Presenter footage, sparse chat UI and dark abstract graphics.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 0–15s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.design: Warm lamps, dark wooden shelves and close-up props.
scenes.purpose: Illustrate a superficial association with photography or colors.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 15–28s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: The visitor examines an old manuscript; a page references color. Disordered books and shelves precede the founder explaining flat indexing and embeddings.
scenes.design: Aged paper, crowded shelves and office presenter.
scenes.purpose: Extend the analogy of irrelevant retrieval.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 28–40s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: A second librarian hears the request, searches the shelves and provides Understanding Exposure.
scenes.design: Warm library views, hand close-ups and a clearly titled book.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 40–51s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Small profile text and vector-like numbers lead to orange cubes in a wireframe space. Labels and text refer to context, relationships, decisions and evolution over time; orange blocks fill more of the frame.
scenes.design: White diagram, fine grid, orange cubes and small contextual text.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 51–59s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: The founder summarizes the promise. The visitor reads in the library under Context to AI, followed by the logo and hydradb.com.
scenes.design: Presenter, library payoff and black end card.
scenes.purpose: Close the metaphor and name the destination.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 59–68.383s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

sound.detail: The draft coherently describes wrong-document retrieval, the library analogy and storing context, relationships and changes over time. Some nouns are misrecognized; visible props and captions support the broad interpretation. Its claims about vector databases are the film’s framing, not verified technical conclusions. No validated listening, delivery, music, effects or sync assessment.
sound.visual_relation: V01–V06; script carries the database explanation.
